newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar ends weaker but off lows.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar ends weaker but off lows.

text.p: CSCE world sugar futures closed a moderately traded session weaker, climbing from early lows on trade shortcovering in October and producer buying in March, dealers said.

Options activity also supported the market above support seen at 11.85 cents a lb in October as trade buying of October calls at the 11.50 strike price prompted the locals who sold the call options to buy futures against the calls, a dealer said.
Liquidation of October and March contracts, and speculators rolling long positions into March ahead of the October contract's end-of-the-month expiry, also kept prices weaker.
"The market came under considerable Oct/March pressure today, which attracted further outright liquidation in October and March, a broker said.
He pegged near-term support basis the October contract at current prices, and at 11.58, the recent low made Sept 5, basis the March contract.
October eased 0.07 cent on the day to close at 11.89, ranging from 12.00 to 11.85. March settled up 0.01 at 11.67, while the remaining months finished 0.01 lower to 0.02 firmer.
LCE white sugar futures ended the day mixed ahead of Friday's expiry of the October contract. The spot month ended up 80 cents a tonne at $346.40.
